Date: Mon, 17 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: No-training commitment and cross-border transfer questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile. Before we move to a pilot contract we'd like to lock down two things for our legal/compliance reviewers: a firm "no training / no model improvement" commitment for customer data, and clarity on cross-border transfer controls (we process EU patient-provided data).

Specifically: 
- A short description of the operational proofs you provide that customer input/output is not used to improve models (evidence we can share with our auditors). 
- Whether subprocessor transfers to third-party model or infra vendors will occur and, if so, whether we can require onshore-only KMS for keys or an on-prem connector.

Can you share an example evidence pack or checklist and an estimate of how long it takes to enable SFTP export + onshore KMS for a Dedicated or Private deployment?

We have a procurement timeline of ~3 weeks; please loop in whoever owns the ops evidence.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morozova
Head of Platform Security | DataCare Health
elena.morozova@datacare.com

Subject: Re: No-training commitment and cross-border transfer questions

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Short answer: we can commit to "no training / no model improvement" for customer-provided data and provide an evidence pack suitable for auditors. Longer answer and next steps below.

Summary of what we can provide immediately:
- Signed DPA exhibit language that prohibits model improvement (we can propose precise wording).
- An operations evidence checklist (see attached template) that maps the controls we operate: request routing, KV/prefix caching policies, telemetry retention settings, and batch/queue policies that exclude customer content from model improvement paths.
- Export mechanisms: SFTP and API exports for customer prompt/response logs; retention and export SLA options documented.
- KMS options: hosted KMS with regional keys + Dedicated/Private deployment support for customer-managed KMS (on-prem/HSM).

Attachments included: redwood-no-train-evidence-template.xlsx (control mapping), sftp-onboarding-steps.docx (ops steps and timing).

Questions to help scope delivery and timeline:
1) Target deployment: Hosted API (fastest) vs Dedicated vs Private (on-prem/VPC). Dedicated/Private add ~3–6 weeks depending on KMS provisioning.
2) Is your requirement to keep keys and logs within the EU, or do you need a fully air-gapped on-prem connector?
3) Any specific subprocessor constraints (we maintain a subprocessor list in our DPA; you can request to block certain vendors)?

Proposed immediate next step: we can kick a 1-week evidence sprint (ops + legal) to produce a tailored evidence pack and a short addendum you can attach to your contract. If that works, Kimberly (ops) will own the delivery; Neha (privacy) will own the contract wording.

Thanks — I can have the initial evidence pack ready by Thu if we have answers to the three scoping questions.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-no-train-evidence-template.xlsx (37 KB), sftp-onboarding-steps.docx (14 KB)

Hi Elena — Kim from Ops here, picking up the evidence sprint that Priyom proposed. Good notes; below are concrete deliverables and realistic timelines based on our standard patterns.

Deliverables we will provide if you sign the addendum: 
- Evidence pack (PDF) with: dataflow diagrams, KV cache eviction policy, batch routing rules, audit log excerpts (last 30 days), and a short ops runbook describing how we enforce the no-train toggle.
- Subprocessor inventory and a proposed subprocessor-restriction appendix (you can nominate up to three vendors to exclude pre-go-live).
- Export proof steps: a test SFTP export within a sandbox tenant and checklist to validate export integrity.
- KMS options: 
  - Option A (Hosted regional KMS): we provision EU-region keys and log access controls.
  - Option B (Customer-managed KMS): we accept wrapped keys from your KMS/HSM; requires Dedicated or Private and an NDA amendment.

Estimated timeline (calendar days after kickoff):
- Evidence pack draft: 3 business days
- SFTP sandbox export test: 5 business days
- KMS integration (customer-managed): 3–4 weeks depending on certs and network setup

Notes on cross-border transfers: We operate regional routing and can restrict storage to EU regions for your tenant. However, some third-party infra vendors may have limited geo-coverage; if you require contractual onshore-only subprocessors we will add those constraints to the DPA but may need a mutual carveout for emergency failover (we can document exact behaviors).

Next steps: 
1) Priyom, can you confirm legal's proposed addendum language and share the initial draft?
2) Elena, please confirm whether you need Option B (customer-managed KMS) or Option A. That decision materially affects the timeline.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Subprocessor restriction: please exclude any China-based infra vendors from processing our tenant. We will supply a short blacklist.
- Evidence pack: contracts@datacare.com would like the initial draft by next Wed to keep procurement on schedule. Deal id is DC-4521.

Two additional asks: 
1) Can you confirm whether metadata (timestamps, IP addresses) tied to prompts/responses are included in the export/evidence pack, and whether those metadata fields are ever used for model telemetry that could feed improvements?
2) On the KMS integration path: do you require a maintenance window or network changes for the Dedicated/Private connector? If so, please outline the expected outage window.

If you can provide answers to 1) and 2) in the initial evidence pack that will unblock our legal team. We can share a short NDA amendment if that helps for key exchange.
